facts.text: The project documentation says the task package defines the gym environment used to train the placing controller
StackingTask is the task in which the robot stacks a given number of parts on an existing structure
BaseTask is the gym.Env base of the task classes
BaseTask.initialize builds observation_space and action_space as gym.spaces.Dict from the sensors and controllers
BaseTask.step returns the legacy four-value tuple observation, reward, done, info
BaseTask.reset takes no seed or options and returns only the initial observation
BaseTask.step ends the episode when the configured time_limit_steps is reached
Controller.initialize returns a normalized gym.spaces.Box action in [-1, 1] per joint
ContinuousSensor normalizes every observation to [-1, 1] and clips only when clip=True
The controller interval of the canonical stacking configuration is 0.05 s and time_limit_steps is round(time_limit_s / controller_interval)
The canonical stacking configuration uses a joint-velocity-difference arm controller and a joint-position gripper controller

The canonical stacking configuration observes the arm joint sin/cos and velocity, the gripper joint angle and velocity, the end-effector pose and velocity, the current part's pose, velocity and target pose, and the time
StackingTask requires controllers, sensors, rewards, a task path, aggregation properties, spawn position and orientation limits and a target position; it has no zero-argument constructor
The episode ends when the last part is released from the gripper, or when the optional target-reached condition is enabled and met
assembly-gym is declared as the git submodule at submodule/assembly-gym

determinism.notes: the fake reseeds random.Random(seed) on reset(seed) and repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; upstream BaseTask.reset takes no seed or options and uses process-global random and numpy generators, so seed control is a property of the fake and was not verified upstream

gaps: analytic kinematics, not a physics engine: no PyBullet, no scene, meshes or task definitions, and no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, gripper mechanics or assembly physics

no UR10 inverse kinematics or controller loop: the fake integrates placeholder joint velocities and an end-effector position; the observation vectors are synthesized normalized state, not sensor readings

the reward and the done condition are placeholders: upstream the reward is a sum of four reward terms and done depends on part release, optional target markers and time_limit_steps (stacking_task.py:142-154, base_task.py:111-112); the fake only stops at a placeholder episode-step count
the observation keys follow the canonical get_env_config sensor set, but the values are not measurements of a simulation and were never compared with an upstream run
the upstream task needs the assembly-gym submodule (.gitmodules:21-24), which is not present in the clone; the fake neither imports it nor the clone
no seed/options contract upstream: BaseTask.reset takes no seed or options (base_task.py:160); the fake accepts a seed for the bridge and ignores reset options
no rendering, snapshot/restore, DIGIT tactile sensors, task data, aggregation properties or wrappers
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; one tick advances the fake by 50 ms, while time_step is a constructor argument upstream and the canonical configuration passes 0.05 s
the sim backend is not offered: the clone registers no gym id and StackingTask cannot be built without the missing submodule and task data; only the fake backend was checked

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: an e-stop latches in the runtime and no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears it; the last state stays readable
